wing.label: relative brightness from PSF wings
wing.method: mean of usable pixels (clean or recovered overflow) in a fixed per-band annulus just outside the target's saturated core in 90% of exposures, minus a local background 4-10 px further out; validated against aperture flux on RW Aur D1 (tests/test_coadd_wings.py): the wing/aperture ratio changes between epochs by x1.23 (median), x1.51 (90th percentile) on unsaturated control stars, so only changes larger than x1.5 are significant. Not a total flux: compare epochs only at similar wavelength (binned_series)

meta.err_note: Empty-sky test: the scatter of flux/err is 1.40, so the listed errors are too small by about that factor.
meta.method: per-exposure circular aperture on the L2 image (MJy/sr x pixel solid angle), sigma-clipped annulus background; err from VARIANCE (or annulus scatter) + background error; masked pixels (any non-informational FLAGS bit except recovered overflow, or no data) are left out and the flux is scaled by the PSF-weighted aperture fraction (truly saturated pixels are kept: lower limit); flagged = more than 15% of the aperture weight masked, or a masked pixel within 1 px of the centre, or a lower limit (masked_fraction per point; on isolated stars, points below 15% with a clean core agree with unmasked ones to a median ratio 0.99-1.00); where OUTLIER pixels were left out, empty-sky fluxes sit 0.3-0.5 sigma low (the outliers removed are the positive ones); saturated = early overflow (OVERFLOW+SUR_ERROR) or NONLINEAR in the aperture: the flux is a lower limit; overflow = recovered overflow pixels (OVERFLOW without SUR_ERROR, slope from the reads before the threshold; recovered/clean flux on RW Aur D1, same epoch and wavelength: median 1.04 over 10 pairs, eight within 1.00-1.20, two at 1.30 and 1.51 near 0.85 um), usable; keep flagged points out of light curves

flag_legend.TRANSIENT: Transient (such as cosmic ray hit) detected during SUR.
flag_legend.OVERFLOW: Overflow threshold reached during SUR. This threshold is set at approximately half the level of full-well saturation.
flag_legend.SUR_ERROR: In the absence of other flags, it indicates a data handling error in the SUR algorithm onboard. When combined with the TRANSIENT or OVERFLOW flags, signals early transient (first half of exposure) or early overflow (first 5 seconds) conditions.
flag_legend.NONFUNC: Static, initially pre-flight assessment that a pixel is permanently unusable/dead.
flag_legend.DICHROIC: This flag indicates pixels with low expected throughput that are not usefully calibratable or of value for photometry.
flag_legend.MISSING_DATA: Pixels for which the onboard data was lost before ingest by the SSDC, e.g., as corrupted packages on the downlink that were not retransmitted successfully, resulting that there is no data available for this pixel in this image.
flag_legend.HOT: Hot pixel - noisy or otherwise affected by spurious signal.
flag_legend.COLD: Pixel that appear unresponsive to light or otherwise has an anomalously low signal in a particular exposure; permanently dead pixels are flagged as NONFUNC.
flag_legend.PERSIST: Pixel found to have been affected by persistent charge above the Level 2 threshold for this.
flag_legend.SOURCE: Pixel mapped to a known source.
flag_legend.BLOOM: Pixel found to have been affected by source blooming (Sect. 3.2.1).

meta.flag_legend_source: SPHEREx Explanatory Supplement v2.1 (2026-11-10, SSDC-DP-017), Table 16 'Image pixel flags used in spectral images at Level 2': one or two sentences of each Description, verbatim
meta.flags_region: flags = names of all FLAGS bits set in any pixel of the measurement region, informational bits (SOURCE, FULLSAMPLE) included: aperture photometry = every pixel the aperture touches; PSF photometry = pixels within 1.5 px of the target (the region that decides 'flagged'). Cutout pixels beyond the detector edge carry MISSING_DATA (set by spx.access)
